exactText: I don’t think we know anything for certain, but I also think we are past the point where recursive self-improvement is science fiction. Instead, it is an explicit item on the roadmap of every major AI company.
sourceQuote: we are past the point where recursive self-improvement is science fiction.
normalizedClaim: Recursive self-improvement of AI is no longer science fiction and is an explicit roadmap item for major AI companies.
resolutionCriteria: Public roadmaps or technical papers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, or similar confirming active work on recursive self-improvement loops by end of 2027.

exactText: whatever AI you're using now is the worst AI you're ever going to use.
sourceQuote: whatever AI you're using now is the worst AI you're ever going to use.
normalizedClaim: Current AI systems will be the worst ones users ever experience going forward due to continued rapid improvement.
resolutionCriteria: Measurable capability improvements in frontier models such that 2025-era systems are clearly inferior on standard benchmarks by 2028.

exactText: Even if the core large language model development stopped right now, there's another ten years of just making it work better with tools and with industry in ways that'll continue to be disruptive.
sourceQuote: there's another ten years of just making it work better with tools and with industry in ways that'll continue to be disruptive.
normalizedClaim: Even if core LLM scaling stopped, tool integration and industry adaptation would produce disruptive progress for another ten years.
resolutionCriteria: Continued significant productivity and process changes from AI tooling in enterprises through 2035, even under a hypothetical scaling slowdown, documented in productivity studies.

exactText: I don't think there's any mass employment from AI, but if you look at where the goal of the AI companies are, it's to be able to build as a machine smarter than a human in the next couple of years to replace all human labor.
sourceQuote: I don't think there's any mass employment from AI
normalizedClaim: There will not be mass unemployment caused by AI in the near term (through ~2027).
resolutionCriteria: U.S. or OECD unemployment rates remaining below levels historically associated with mass technological unemployment through 2027, per BLS/OECD data.

exactText: Starting in late 2025, we entered a new era thanks to AI agents like Claude Code , OpenAI’s Codex, and OpenClaw. These are AI systems that you can just give work to, sometimes hours of human work, and get back reasonable and useful results in minutes.
sourceQuote: we entered a new era thanks to AI agents
normalizedClaim: Late 2025 marked the beginning of a new era defined by practical AI agents capable of completing hours of human work.
resolutionCriteria: Widespread recognition in industry analyses and adoption metrics that 2025–2026 constituted the transition to usable long-horizon AI agents.

exactText: Right now, the doubling time for capability is about every five to nine months, which is an exceptionally fast doubling time.
sourceQuote: the doubling time for capability is about every five to nine months
normalizedClaim: AI capability is currently doubling approximately every 5–9 months.
resolutionCriteria: Independent measurements of frontier model capability (e.g., METR time-horizon or similar benchmarks) showing continued doubling in the 5–9 month range through 2027.

exactText: It's going to move, I think, increasingly inside organizations. We're seeing organizational adoption increase as well.
sourceQuote: It's going to move, I think, increasingly inside organizations.
normalizedClaim: AI use will increasingly shift from individual chatbot interactions to deeper integration inside organizational processes.
resolutionCriteria: Enterprise surveys (Gartner, McKinsey, etc.) showing majority of AI value coming from process redesign and agentic workflows rather than standalone chat by 2028.

exactText: If the loop does close, the exponential curves we’ve been watching would get steeper, with an uncertain endpoint.
sourceQuote: If the loop does close, the exponential curves we’ve been watching would get steeper
normalizedClaim: If recursive self-improvement loops close, the rate of AI capability improvement will accelerate beyond current exponential trends.
resolutionCriteria: Observable acceleration in capability benchmarks beyond prior doubling rates following confirmed recursive improvement systems, by 2030.

exactText: I think that's a dangerous view because it isn't static. It's evolving.
normalizedClaim: AI progress is not static; capabilities will continue evolving disruptively.
resolutionCriteria: Continued measurable year-over-year gains in frontier model capabilities through at least 2028.

exactText: We can see the shape of the Thing now, but we can still influence the Thing itself, and what it means for all of us.
sourceQuote: we can still influence the Thing itself
normalizedClaim: Human choices in the near term can still meaningfully shape the trajectory and societal impact of advanced AI.
resolutionCriteria: Observable divergence in AI deployment outcomes, governance regimes, or capability emphasis across organizations/countries by 2030 attributable to deliberate policy and design choices.
